description:
Found s504 by s501t while bisecting the op/tiehandle.t "11/32 -> TIMEOUT 1/5" companion mover.

MEASURED (2026-10-02, load ~2.5):
- s501t tree f027754a, `tools/run-perl-suite.pl --jobs 1 op/tiehandle.t` with stdin = the tool's (closed/empty): C 11/32 DIFF, three runs.
- same tree, `sleep 200 | tools/run-perl-suite.pl --jobs 1 op/tiehandle.t`: TIMEOUT 1/5.
- BASE a0899ba6 extraction, same `sleep 200 |` spelling: TIMEOUT 1/5 too.
So it is NOT a regression of s501t; the s501t "after" companion run (2026-10-01 01:42) was taken with an open stdin, the "before" with a closed one.

CAUSE: the PCL child inherits the runner's stdin.  op/tiehandle.t line 298 ties *ARGV (`local *ARGV; @ARGV=('haha'); tie *ARGV,'Implement'`); PCL leaves a filehandle untied (#2590, announced), so the following `eof()` / `eof` consult the real ARGV chain -> STDIN, which blocks until the timeout when stdin is an open pipe.  The PCL TAP up to row 44 was on disk (44 rows), but the TIMEOUT path counts 1/5.

FIX OPTIONS: (a) the runner spawns the PCL (and perl) children with `< /dev/null` -- perl's own harness reads tests with a terminal/none; a runner change => re-run the runner once and compare verdicts file by file (WHAT-TO-RUN-WHEN "runners" row).  (b) nothing until #2590 lands (then the tie is real and STDIN is never read).
Until then: run companion legs with `< /dev/null`.
subject: run-perl-suite.pl hands its OWN stdin to the PCL child: op/tiehandle.t blocks reading real STDIN (dropped tie *ARGV, #2590) and TIMEOUTs whenever the runner stdin is an open pipe
